items.title: Norm of a self adjoint operator from its quadratic form
items.design_obligation: (lemma) — $\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|=1}|\langle Tx,x\rangle|$
items.strategy: Polarize the Hermitian form and rescale two vectors to prove the upper bound for the operator norm; the reverse inequality is Cauchy–Schwarz. Handle the zero Hilbert space separately with supremum defined as zero.

items.design_obligation: (lemma) — compactness turns a maximizing sequence into a norm-convergent image subsequence
items.strategy: Choose approximate quadratic maximizers, pass to one sign, show (T-lambda I)x_n tends to zero for lambda=plus or minus norm(T), and use convergence of Tx_n to obtain a unit eigenvector. Require T nonzero; no assertion about a zero-space eigenvector.

items.title: Orthogonal complement of an eigenspace is invariant

items.title: Spectral theorem for compact self adjoint operators
items.design_obligation: (theorem) — nonzero real eigenvalues of finite multiplicity tend only to zero, and their eigenspaces span $\overline{\operatorname{ran}T}$
items.strategy: Iterate the extremal eigenvector construction on invariant orthogonal complements. Compactness excludes infinitely many orthonormal eigenvectors with eigenvalues bounded away from zero. The residual restriction vanishes; identify the support with closure of the range. No basis of the possibly nonseparable kernel is selected.

items.title: Positive square root of a compact positive operator
items.design_obligation: (lemma) — the compact self-adjoint expansion gives a unique compact positive $S$ with $S^2=T$, including the kernel and the possible accumulation at zero
items.strategy: On each positive eigenspace multiply by the scalar square root and vanish on the kernel. Norm truncations prove compactness. For uniqueness a positive square root commutes with T, preserves each eigenspace, and vanishes on ker(T); on a positive eigenspace positivity excludes the negative scalar root.

items.title: Fa5 singular values equal approximation numbers
items.statement: For compact Hilbert-space T, s_n(T)=inf_{rank F<n}||T-F||, with zero padding.
items.strategy: SVD truncation gives the upper bound. On the span of the first n right singular vectors rank(F)<n gives a unit vector killed by F, yielding the lower bound. Use no general Banach-space approximation property.

items.statement: For a bounded Hilbert-space operator T, T is compact iff a_n(T)=inf{||T-F||:rank(F)<n} tends to zero. For compact T, a_n(T)=s_n(T), with zero padding.

items.title: Continuous functions form a commutative banach algebra
items.statement: For nonempty compact Hausdorff K prove C(K,C) is a unital commutative Banach algebra under the supremum norm; spectrum of f is f(K).
items.strategy: For nonempty compact Hausdorff K prove C(K,C) is a unital commutative Banach algebra under the supremum norm; spectrum of f is f(K).

items.title: Bounded operators form a noncommutative banach algebra
items.statement: For nonzero complex Banach X, B(X) is a unital Banach algebra; use C2 matrix units for a concrete noncommutative example.

items.title: Spectrum in a finite dimensional matrix algebra
items.design_obligation: — eigenvalues and determinant
items.statement: In M_n(C), spectrum equals zeros of det(lambda I-A); verify the inverse via adjugates when determinant is nonzero.
items.strategy: In M_n(C), spectrum equals zeros of det(lambda I-A); verify the inverse via adjugates when determinant is nonzero.

items.title: Spectrum of a multiplication operator
items.design_obligation: — essential range, citing MT measure notions
items.statement: For a bounded measurable multiplier on L2 of a sigma-finite measure space the spectrum is its essential range. Construct approximate eigenvectors on positive finite-measure subsets where |m-lambda| is small. Specify the zero measure/zero algebra exception.

items.title: Spectrum of the unilateral shift
items.design_obligation: — closed unit disk, with point/approximate/residual behavior separated
items.statement: For S e_n=e_(n+1) on ell2(N0), spectrum is the closed unit disk, point spectrum empty, residual and compression spectra the open disk, continuous and approximate point spectra the unit circle. Prove the lower bound inside the disk, adjoint eigenvectors there, and normalized long blocks at the boundary.

items.design_obligation: — a nonzero nilpotent
items.statement: For the 2 by 2 matrix E_12, square is zero, norm is one and spectrum is {0}.

items.title: Spectrum can shrink in a larger banach algebra
items.design_obligation: — state the unital-subalgebra hypotheses
items.statement: Use the disk algebra embedded by boundary restriction in C(unit circle): the coordinate function has spectrum closed disk in the first algebra and circle in the second. Prove closedness and completeness of the disk algebra and the maximum-modulus norm identity; required supplier audit remains open.

items.title: Unitization of a nonunital banach algebra
items.design_obligation: — multiplication, norm choice, and spectrum convention
items.statement: For a nonunital Banach algebra A define A~=C direct sum A, multiplication (lambda,a)(mu,b)=(lambda mu,lambda b+mu a+ab), norm |lambda|+||a||. Verify associativity and completeness and use this named unitization for spectra.

items.title: Riesz projection for a matrix with separated spectrum
items.statement: For diag(1,2), integrate the diagonal resolvent around 1 to obtain diag(1,0); check both invariant summands.
